prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: warehouse receiving to outbound load release. Elements: Yard Gate Controller=Velvetrook (records vehicle/carrier/trailer/arrival; validates vs receiving plan; flags unscheduled; directs to door; uses Trailer Seal Exception Note; blocks risky vehicles; recovery: holds vehicles outside boundary). Inbound Inspection Desk=Cinderbay (checks paperwork/seals; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note; records proceed/rework/hold). Pallet Dimension Scanner=Moonquarry (produces Oversize Load Advisory; checks profiles vs limits, flags out-of-tolerance; never authorizes rule-violating placement). Inbound Pallet Buffer (staging only). North/South Aisle Stacker Crane (North=Juniperwake: sends Aisle Occupancy Snapshot to WMS; uses Slot Reservation Receipt; verifies clearance before resuming; stops on obstruction/invalid path). East/West Transfer Conveyor (interlocked; East restart: one empty reduced-speed cycle; record authorization, speed, cycle result, alarm response). Conveyor Line Controller=Brasshaven (produces Transfer Induction Ticket; inhibits feed on incomplete restart, protective-device change, unsafe downstream, isolated area). Autonomous Forklift Fleet=Larkspur (receives Transfer Induction Ticket, validates destination vs route; produces Forklift Handoff Confirmation). Outbound Dispatch Sorter (receives Dispatch Wave Amendment). Outbound Checkweigh Scale (Gross Weight Variance Slip; reference-load check at shift start/after maintenance). Shipping Documentation Desk. Safety Zone Controller, Fire Alarm Panel (Sprinkler Zone Inhibit Notice; SZC keeps exclusion boundary until release criteria; both may stop movement). Maintenance Release Terminal=Copperfield (Crane Service Release Card; status checked before automatic service). Warehouse Management System=Morrowglass: authoritative; produces Slot Reservation Receipt; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment; records transaction times, reconciles vs shift plan. Actor: Warehouse Operations Supervisor (shift-start review of alarms/equipment/unresolved work; confirms operator awareness of speed limits/boundaries/stop-work; compares downtime vs event records, investigates differences; releases work after reconciliation). Requirements: no work without WMS release; unique task ref; held pallets separated; dimensional exceptions held; safety checks before production movement; boundaries visible/enforced. Recovery mode: aisle restricted; staged resumption observed. KPIs: throughput, completion time, availability, exceptions, route delays; near misses reviewed.

Document units:
S217: At handover, the outgoing shift records equipment restrictions, pending checks, and unresolved safety concerns.
S218: The incoming shift acknowledges those conditions before authorizing routine movements.
S219: Commissioning acceptance is conducted against an approved test plan before routine warehouse operation begins.
S220: The test plan defines expected behavior, safety limits, evidence requirements, and criteria for blocking release.
S221: Each subsystem is exercised under representative loads, including recovery from interrupted transactions and controlled equipment stops.
S222: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor confirms that acceptance evidence is complete and that any remaining limitations are documented.
S223: The Warehouse Management System is checked for inventory accuracy, transaction integrity, and correct handling of unavailable storage locations.
S224: Acceptance is withheld when a material defect could compromise personnel safety, inventory control, or shipment accuracy.
S225: The Warehouse Management System uses the handoff confirmation to close the applicable movement record.
S226: The Shipping Documentation Desk receives and reconciles the Gross Weight Variance Slip against the applicable shipment record before completing its paperwork.
S227: A scale variance outside the approved tolerance is investigated and resolved before the affected shipment is released.
S228: The North Aisle Stacker Crane accepts the release card as authorization to return to service after its checks are complete.
S229: A crane remains unavailable for automated assignments until its functional checks and required safety checks have passed.
S230: Morrowglass closes the commissioning action register only after unresolved findings have named owners and due dates.
S231: Cinderbay records governance approval and confirms that the accepted operating configuration is under change control.
S232: Brasshaven verifies that conveyor zones are clear and records the completion of its assigned closing checks.
S233: Larkspur parks its vehicles in approved locations and reports any remaining equipment restrictions for the next shift.
S234: Copperfield records completed service work and confirms that equipment restrictions remain visible until formally cleared.
S235: The Fire Alarm Panel is checked for active faults, bypasses, and indications requiring escalation before the facility is released.
S236: The Safety Zone Controller is verified against the approved access boundaries and stop-response behavior.
S237: The Inbound Inspection Desk and Outbound Dispatch Sorter confirm that their operating interfaces are available and that exceptions can be held safely.
S238: Changes to software, equipment settings, or operating procedures require an impact review, approval, and a controlled implementation record.
S239: Emergency changes are documented promptly and reviewed by the Warehouse Operations Supervisor before normal operation resumes.
